reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency asks for an estimated product obtained by rounding factors to multiples of 10, but seed 42 asks 'What is 15 x 2?' and keys the exact value 30 - the competency-correct estimate would be 20 x 2 = 40. Seeds 44 and 45 ask only 'Round 12 to the nearest 10.' (keyed 10, correct in isolation), which is a place-value sub-skill, not an estimated product.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The composite skill named by the wording - round both factors, then multiply the rounded values - is never rendered in any of the five seeds. There is no 3-digit factor, no 2-digit multiplier, and no item that chains the rounding step to a multiplication step.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentence structure and vocabulary are readable, but 'What is 17 x 0?' (seed 43) and 'What is 23 x 0?' (seed 46) are zero-property recall from Grade 1-2 and demand no estimation reasoning at all, leaving the cognitive load far under what a Grade 3 Quarter 3 estimation lesson should carry.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Seeds 44 and 45 produce the same stem, 'Round 12 to the nearest 10.', and seeds 43 and 46 are the same 'two-digit x 0' template. No 'about how many' phrasing, no real-world estimation context, and no compare-the-estimate-to-the-exact variant appears anywhere.

competency_alignment.rationale: The sampled items split into two unrelated skills - isolated rounding (seeds 44, 45) and exact multiplication (seeds 42, 43, 46) - with no item joining them. A pupil working this ladder never practises the target behaviour, so the progression cannot build this competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The stated range is 2- to 3-digit numbers multiplied by 1- to 2-digit numbers. Observed factor pairs are 15 x 2, 17 x 0 and 23 x 0: no 3-digit number ever appears, the multiplier never exceeds 2, and two of three multipliers are 0, which collapses the estimation task entirely.
